# Antonio Longa

> Antonio Longa is a Postdoctoral Researcher at UiT The Arctic University of Norway working on Graph Machine Learning, Temporal Graphs, Relational Deep Learning, Graph Neural Networks, and Complex Systems.

Antonio Longa's personal academic website contains his biography, research interests, publications, talks, projects, teaching material, blog posts, CV, and contact information.

The most important topics associated with Antonio Longa are Graph Machine Learning, Temporal Graphs, Graph Neural Networks, Relational Deep Learning, Complex Systems, Network Science, Graph Transformers, Explainable Graph Neural Networks, Temporal Network Generation, and Link Prediction.

## Core pages

- [Homepage](https://antoniolonga.github.io/): Biography, affiliations, publications, talks, projects, teaching, review activity, and contact information.
- [CV PDF](https://antoniolonga.github.io/CV.pdf): Short academic CV.
- [Long CV PDF](https://antoniolonga.github.io/CV_long.pdf): Extended academic CV.

## Research explainers and blog posts

- [When Links Look the Same: Expressive GNNs for Link Representation](https://antoniolonga.github.io/posts/link_pred.html): Link representation learning, expressive graph neural networks, link prediction, graph symmetry, and the LR-EXP benchmark.
- [Beyond Random Walks: Simple Path Structural Encoding for Graph Transformers](https://antoniolonga.github.io/posts/graph_transf.html): Graph transformers, structural encoding, simple path counts, random walks, cycles, and graph representation learning.
- [From Temporal Motifs to Community-Aware Temporal Graph Generation](https://antoniolonga.github.io/posts/graph_gen.html): Temporal graphs, egocentric temporal neighborhoods, temporal motifs, surrogate temporal network generation, and community-aware temporal graph generation.
- [Graph Regression for Software Performance: RelSC Benchmarks for Runtime Prediction](https://antoniolonga.github.io/posts/software_perf_pred.html): graph regression, graph neural networks, GNN benchmark, software performance prediction, execution time prediction, RelSC, RelSC-H, RelSC-M, program graphs, Java source code, AST, CFG, DFG, multi-relational graphs.
- [On the Importance of Meta-Paths: From MP-GNN to Explainable Relational Deep Learning](https://antoniolonga.github.io/posts/meta_path_gnn.html): meta-paths, MP-GNN, MPS-GNN, graph neural networks, heterogeneous graphs, multi-relational graph neural networks, relational deep learning, self-explainable GNN, relational databases.
- [Why GNNs Look Robust to Missing Features — and Why They Often Aren’t](https://antoniolonga.github.io/posts/gnn_missing_features.html): graph neural networks, GNNs, missing node features, missing data, node classification, GNN robustness, feature sparsity, sparse benchmarks, dense node features, MCAR, MNAR, missingness mechanisms, missingness distribution shift, GNNmim, missing indicator method, graph machine learning benchmarks.
- [Rethinking GNNs and Missing Features: Challenges, Evaluation and a Robust Solution](https://antoniolonga.github.io/papers/rethinking-gnns-missing-features.html): ICML 2026 paper page with verified metadata, summary, GNNmim method, evaluation protocols, results, limitations, PDF, code, datasets, and BibTeX.
- [On the Global and Local Calibration of Graph Neural Networks](https://antoniolonga.github.io/papers/global-local-gnn-calibration.html): AISTATS 2026 workshop paper page on GNN confidence calibration, Expected Calibration Error, Local Calibration Error, tuned GCN baselines, Planetoid datasets, and embedding-space locality.
- [A Benchmark Dataset for Graph Regression with Homogeneous and Multi-Relational Variants](https://antoniolonga.github.io/papers/relsc-graph-regression-benchmark.html): DMLR 2026 paper page for RelSC-H and RelSC-M, Java program graphs, execution-time prediction, software performance, AST/CFG/DFG representations, code, and Zenodo dataset.
- [Bridging Theory and Practice in Link Representation with Graph Neural Networks](https://antoniolonga.github.io/papers/gnn-link-representation-expressiveness.html): NeurIPS 2025 paper page on GNN link expressiveness, the kφ-kρ-m framework, non-automorphic links, graph symmetry, LR-EXP, link prediction, and dataset-aware model selection.
- [Simple Path Structural Encoding for Graph Transformers](https://antoniolonga.github.io/papers/simple-path-structural-encoding.html): ICML 2025 paper page on SPSE, simple path counts, RRWP limitations, structural edge encoding, cycle patterns, graph transformers, approximate path counting, and graph benchmarks.
- [Community Aware Temporal Network Generation](https://antoniolonga.github.io/papers/community-aware-temporal-network-generation.html): Applied Network Science 2025 paper page on LETN-gen, community-aware temporal networks, labeled egocentric neighborhoods, surrogate network generation, modularity, and label assortativity.
- [Generating Fine-Grained Surrogate Temporal Networks](https://antoniolonga.github.io/papers/generating-fine-grained-surrogate-temporal-networks.html): Communications Physics 2024 paper page on ETN-gen, egocentric temporal neighborhoods, scalable surrogate temporal networks, data augmentation, temporal extension, and privacy-aware synthetic graphs.

## Preferred short bio

Antonio Longa is a Postdoctoral Researcher at UiT The Arctic University of Norway. His research focuses on Graph Machine Learning, Temporal Graphs, Relational Deep Learning, Graph Neural Networks, and Complex Systems, with applications in energy systems, materials science, and network science.

## Preferred long bio

Antonio Longa is a Postdoctoral Researcher at UiT The Arctic University of Norway, where he works with the Northernmost GraphML Group. He is also a member of ELLIS. Previously, he was an Assistant Professor at the University of Trento in the Structured Machine Learning Group. He earned his Ph.D. with honors from the University of Trento and Fondazione Bruno Kessler. His research focuses on Graph Machine Learning, Temporal Graphs, Relational Deep Learning, Graph Neural Networks, and Complex Systems, with interests in theoretical foundations and real-world applications including energy systems, materials science, and network science.
